title: Deeper/broader ModelDocViewStyle dictionary hierarchy and property-completeness review
mode: Primary Autodesk API documentation review plus local source/test audit; plan update only
head: de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
scope: Verify the documented NOD ownership graph for DETAILVIEWSTYLE and SECTIONVIEWSTYLE.
Compare the required graph with the current generated ASCII/Binary test and fileExport preflight.
Screen the style property inventories against local typed fields and refine the existing PAR-20 implementation order.

method.kind: Read-only primary-source web review and local source audit; research receipt and plan edited
method.limitations: Autodesk ObjectARX documentation directly establishes that the ACAD_*VIEWSTYLE NOD key resolves to a dictionary containing style objects, and its public property inventories provide semantic completeness prompts. These sources do not define every DXF field order or DWG byte layout. The local generated test/source were inspected but not rerun or repaired in this research pass.

sources.observed: The database methods open an AcDbDictionary beneath the ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE or ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE NOD key; the dictionary contains the matching style objects. Autodesk's dictionary example shows these keys with named child records and describes each dictionary entry as a key plus a hard-ownership reference.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Authoritative API/object ownership hierarchy and dictionary-entry semantics; not a complete DXF record schema, version matrix, DWG byte layout, or native round-trip result.

sources.observed: The documented semantic property inventories include show/display controls, style/resource identifiers, colors, sizes, line settings, label settings, and section hatching controls. Local classes retain some flags or unnamed booleans, so every property needs an explicit field/flag/opaque-preservation/unsupported disposition before typed completeness is claimed.
sources.evidenceCeiling: Property-semantic inventory only. Property names do not establish DXF group-code mapping or DWG encoding.

localCrosswalk.owner: PAR-20/7G.3f.4b.2 ModelDocViewStyle graph and same-version replay
localCrosswalk.observed: The current generated control stores ACAD_DETAILVIEWSTYLE and ACAD_SECTIONVIEWSTYLE directly in the NOD with handles 0x105/0x106; each style record names NOD handle 0xC as parent. The fileExport root admission accepts exactly a typed style object whose owner is the NOD and emits the style handle under the root key. Autodesk's documented graph instead requires the root key to identify a DICTIONARY, whose child key identifies the style object.
localCrosswalk.disposition: Confirmed local graph/test contract defect. The prior same-codec replay result is self-consistency evidence only; reopen the same-version structural replay slice and replace the generated graph plus exporter/import-evidence hierarchy before claiming valid root closure.

localCrosswalk.observed: Local detail/section style classes contain broad typed payloads, flags, and two unnamed section booleans; the public API property lists include additional named display toggles. No qualified typed style serializer exists in this slice.
localCrosswalk.disposition: Readiness/completeness question, not an additional confirmed wire defect. Build a property-to-wire/flag matrix from authoritative schema or admitted producer traces; do not infer bit/code assignments from API names.

assessment.planEffect: Correct implementation order: first represent NOD-to-style-dictionary and dictionary-to-style named ownership, then validate typed/raw receipt and resource closure, then remap/output and verify complete normalized raw replay. Keep DWG-origin serialization and native model-view rendering blocked on their separate gates.
